items: The greatest heroes and sacrifices are memorialized throughout the city. Learning more about these monuments and the incidents they immortalize could help in understanding the community of Metropolis.
This collection is comprised by seven plaque rubbings that recall past events that occurred in Metropolis and its inhabitants prior to the beginning of the events in DC Universe Online.

sections.title: Death and Return of Superman
items: The Superman Statue was erected in Centennial Park as a memorial for Superman following his death while stopping Doomsday, an artificial lifeform created by a Kryptonian scientist long before its destruction.

Meant to be the Ultimate form of life, he was purposefully killed only for the scientist to resurrect him by putting together whatever pieces survived, in an attempt to create a stronger, more resistant version of him. The Ultimate eventually developed the natural ability of enduring any threats he faced in prior lives without further technological intervention, killed all the scientists in the lab (including his creator), escaped ancient Krypton. The indestructible being eventually found its way to Earth, where he faced the Justice League America*, Superman included. They fought an epic battle that culminated with Superman sacrificing himself to stop Doomsday from destroying all living beings on Earth. He was buried in Centennial Park next to his statue.

Jonathan Kent, Superman's father, briefly died due to a heart attack triggered the grief of losing his only son). He meets with his son in the afterlife and convinces him to return to the world of living. Superman's essence returned to his body just when the Eradicator (an ancient Kryptonian living weapon created by one of Kal-El's anscetors) attempted possess his body. As Kal-El's body was not an empty shell anymore, the Eradicator took him to the Fortress of Solitude, placing him within a Kryptonian Regeneration Matrix so he could use Superman to absorb the Sun's power. However the Matrix could not contain that amount of power and broke open, allowing the weakened Superman to escape.

sections.title: Justice League: New World Order
items: The Martian Invasion Plaque was created to memorialise an attempted invasion of Earth by White Martians.

One day, a mysterious flying saucer arrived near the White House, and the president of the United States called for the Justice League*. Superman arrived just as the saucer laid eight metallic eggs, and out of them came a group of superpowerful aliens who called themselves the Hyperclan. They claimed to be from a planet that had been destroyed by its own inhabitants, and their mission was to prevent other planets from meeting the same fate by fixing them. Humanity immediately accepted the group's intervention, but the League got suspicious of their intentions. The Hyperclan's first act was to transform the Sahara Desert into an Eden, skyrocketing their popularity. Superman advised people to take a more cynical approach to the newcomers, but he is accused of being envious, as the Hyperclan was able to fix the world in a way the superheroes never could. When the Hyperclan started executing villains, the supercrime figures decreased dramatically.

In space, the Justice League Refuge is attacked by beings that seem to have materialized outside the station. They attacked the satellite's hull, and Wonder Woman and Green Lantern Kyle Rayner (a recent addition to the team after having worked with the Titans) go outside to stop them. Metamorpho decided to use his body as a shuttle to save Icemaiden, Nuklon, and Obsidian. Wonder Woman and Green Lantern were unable to prevent the destruction of Refuge, and the team that had escaped to Earth managed to survive - except for Metamorpho, who was deemed "inert" after the impact. In the Antarctic, the Hyperclan unearths a Martian city named Z'onn Z'orr.

The JLA blamed the Hyperclan for the attack, who denied any involvement, accusing the League of manufacturing a confrontation. Superman, Wonder Woman, and Green Lantern reunite with Batman, Flash, and Martian Manhunter in the Secret Sanctuary in Rhode Island ( Aquaman ignores the call). Batman suspected that the Hyperclan had been using radio frequencies to control the minds of Earth's population, which Superman is able to confirm — it's a planned invasion, and they're actively turning the world against the Justice League. Meanwhile, two stations mysteriously appear - one in Mongolia's Gobi Desert, and another above the Pacific Ocean near Midway Island. After some investigation, Superman confirmed that the flying saucer in Washington was nothing more than a projection. They split to tackle the three structures, but the Martian sneaked away to have a meeting with Protex, Hyperclan's leader, deciding to join them. Flash and Green Lantern find that the frequencies are being transmitted from the dozens of ships hidden in hyperspace. The League is captured and taken to Z'onn Z'orr, and Batman is believed to be dead. The Dark Knight figured out what kind of aliens they were dealing with: Martians; he invades the city and takes down four of the Hyperclan members with fire. After that, the Martians decide to begin the invasion early.

Once Superman heard people asking for help all over the world, he asked himself why he wasn't dead already, as the kryptonite the Hyperclan was using to weaken him should have killed him at that point. Then, he realized that all metahumans with fire powers got sick, and that their powers are the same as Martian Manhunter's - who reveals himself as one of the members in disguise, the real one still in the desert. They free the rest of the League, and the team defeats the remaining members of the clan. Superman transmits a message to let the world know they can repel the invasion using fire. People all over the world light up matches and lighters, and the White Martians retreat. The League gets to the Still Zone, where the Whites' ships were hidden, and Martian Manhunter brainwashes them into believing they are humans and sends them to live on Earth as ordinary people.

sections.title: Superman: For Tomorrow
items: The Vanishing Plaque was created to memorialise an incident where a million people mysteriously disappeared from the planet.

While Superman was in space helping Green Lantern Kyle Rayner, one million people disappeared from various locations around the globe, including his wife, Lois Lane. The feelings of guilt (for being absent during the event) and grief (for losing Lois) dominated him. While dealing with a conflict in a Middle Eastern country, he found the weapon responsible for the Vanishing: a strange metallic sphere used by the revolutionary forces, granted to them by an unknown benefactor along with a living weapon named Equus. Equus went rogue when Superman attempted to confiscate the weapon, attacking the hero before activating the machine for the second time - causing the world to blink, and 300,000 people to disappear, including himself. As Superman was the only witness to the event, the other members of the Justice League* suspected him of his part in the event, but gave him a chance. Back in the Fortress of Solitude, he studied the device and found out it was a creation of his own.

Worried about the future of the Earth might be similar to Krypton's, Superman had decided to create an idyllic dimension inside the Phantom Zone (created by his biological father, Jor-El), a refuge that he named Metropia, and only Lois was aware of its existence. Once he had stepped into that new world, he concluded that no man, super or not, has the right to create such a thing. Lois had convinced him that the place should be preserved, but as a secret between the two of them. Superman created automatons in the likeness of his biological parents and his civilian identity to serve as guardians, then sent them and the key (the metallic sphere), and erased his own memories related to the project. But the key was found...by General Zod. Zod was the one behind the Vanishing - it was all a plan to reach Superman so he could kill him.

Superman fixed the key so it won't teleport people randomly, and entered Metropia with no intention of returning. Reuniting with Lois and the automatons, he learned that Zod wants to rule the place, and he now has Equus on his side. As the two Kryptonians fought, Superman realized that each hit they dealt to each other damaged the very world he created - both of them were part of the fabric of Metropia. He uses the key to open a portal so people can escape the destruction. Superman tries to save Zod, but the villain is sucked deeper into the Phantom Zone. The people who survive Zod's attack return to Earth, reverting the Vanishing.

sections.title: Infinite Crisis
items: By the end of the Crisis on Infinite Earths, only one Earth remained. There was only one positive universe, known as New Earth, and an Antimatter Universe. The Multiverse no longer existed. All counterparts of each person in an alternative reality became one, with the exception of four refugees: Alex Luthor from Earth-Three, Superboy-Prime from Earth-Prime (not to be confused with Prime Earth), and Superman (Kal-L) and Lois Lane-Kent from Earth-Two. Alex created a timeless crystalline pocket-dimension for them from which they could watch the past of former Earths, as well as observe the heroes of New Earth, and judged them undeserving of being the version preserved in the new universe, a universe that they allowed to become more and more evil. On top of that, Lois Kent was suffering from a mysterious degenerative disease. They decided they had to recreate the multiverse to get rid of the tainted Earth and save Lois - or at least that was what Alex Luthor wanted them to believe; his real plan was to recreate the multiverse so he could combine elements of each of them to make a perfect Earth. For that, they operated in secrecy throughout the universe to spread chaos and contempt, took over the Brother Eye satellite, and built a tower in the Fortress of Solitude out of the Anti-Monitor's dead body to work as a cosmic tuning fork powered by super beings who are originally from different Earths: Martian Manhunter (Earth-One), Power Girl (Earth-Two), Black Adam (Earth-S), Nightshade (Earth-Four), Lady Quark (Earth-Six), Breach (Earth-Eight), and The Ray (Earth-X).

sections.title: Superboy: Touchdown
items: The Superboy Statue was erected as a memorial for Superboy following his death during Infinite Crisis.

Superboy-Prime (Kal-El) came from Earth-Prime, a version of the very that is very similar to ours - DC Comics is a real publishing company, and all of the characters in the DC Universe are fictional, including Superman. Expect that the planet Krypton actually existed, and it was about to be destroyed by its red sun. The scientists Jor-El and Lara decided to save their son Kal-El by sending him away. Kal-El materialized in a forest in a New England seacoast town, where he was found by computer programmer Jerry Kent and attorney Naomi Clarke Kent. The couple adopted the toddler and named him after Superman's civilian identity, Clark. He grew up without superpowers until his teenage years, when he pretended to be Superman and found out he was actually able to fly like his namesake. But that coincided with the Crisis of Infinite Earths, and Earth-Prime was destroyed, but Superboy-Prime was saved by the Monitor.

The years Superboy-Prime spent in the pocket-dimension caused him homesickness and to resent the heroes of New Earth, as they were deeply flawed in comparison to the fictional heroes of his Earth. He especially envied Superboy's life: Conner had a family, friends, a girlfriend, and a life, but wasn't a real hero; he carried the genes of Lex Luthor. Superboy-Prime attacks Superboy, beating him and Krypto badly, but they are rescued by the Titans, the Doom Patrol, and the Justice Society - as Superboy-Prime didn't have much experience with his own powers, he ended up maiming and brutally murdering some of the heroes, until he was stopped by the male speedsters: Wally West, Jay Garrick, and Kid Flash ran the enraged villain into the Speed Force, where they were aided by the souls of Barry Allen, Johnny Quick, and Max Mercury. Superboy is placed in a healing chamber by Lex Luthor, who gave him a crystal from the pocket dimension that could point to the location of Alex Luthor's tower. Meanwhile, Superboy-Prime escaped the speedsters, and Alex Luthor began to split the Earths and test them. Superman and Lois returned to their Earth-Two, but she died anyway; Kal-L blamed Superman from New Earth for her death, but Wonder Woman intervenes and they have a conversation that made Kal-L realize that he was used by Alex Luthor.

Still weakened, Superboy leaves the chamber to help Nightwing get to the tower so they can disable it, and Wonder Girl joins them there. The trio faces a legion of OMACs, and they're able to free the prisoners. That's when Superboy-Prime arrives. He reveals to Luthor that the Flashes had traveled back in time and imprisoned him under a red sun, and he used parts of the Anti-Monitor to build himself an armor that feeds him yellow sunlight. As they fought away from the tower, the former prisoners were sent back to their respective Earths. The Superboys had a rematch that ended with Conner grabbing Superboy-Prime and the two flying towards the tower, causing an explosion that pulled all of the Earths back together into a single one. Conner stayed alive for long enough to know he saved the universe before succumbing to the injuries.

sections.title: Battle of Metropolis: Finale
items: The Battle of Metropolis Memorial was created to memorialise the final, colossal battle between Earth's heroes and villains in Metropolis at the end of the Infinite Crisis.

The Society gathered every villain and declared war on the heroes - if they were able to conquer Metropolis, the rest of the world would fall too. That was Alex Luthor's contingency plan; since he couldn't build the perfect world by combining multiple Earths, he would take over New Earth and make it perfect by force. Heroes and villains fight each other, but the only thing Superboy-Prime wanted was his Earth-Prime back. With the tower destroyed, that was impossible, so he decided he was going to fly through Oa at the speed of light to trigger another Big Bang, so the universe would restart, and he would be the only one with superpowers. Martian Manhunter read his mind and called for the heroes who could fly after Superboy-Prime to stop him. The Green Lanterns were able to slow him down just in time for the two Supermen to put their plan in action. They flew Superboy across Krypton's remains (made of Kryptonite), then through the red sun, until they landed on Mogo. The weakened Kryptonians continued to fight; Superboy killed Superman from Earth-Two, but Superman of New Earth was able to defeat the villain just as the cavalry arrived. The Green Lanterns and Donna Troy trapped Superboy-Prime inside a junior red-sun eater surrounded by a quantum containment field, with fifty Lanterns watching him incessantly.

Back in Metropolis, Batman defeated Deathstroke. When Alex Luthor hurt Nightwing, Batman took Deathstroke pistol and pointed it at Alex. Wonder Woman breaks her sword and convinces Batman that killing Luthor is not worth it. As they walk away, an avalanche of rubble buries Luthor, but the two heroes are not sure he's dead. With Superboy-Prime and Alex Luthor out, the heroes won the Battle of Metropolis. A few days later, the reconstruction began.

Alex Luthor didn't die during the battle. He managed to get to Gotham City with the intention of trying to "save" the Earth again. But he underestimated the nemesis of two of the greatest heroes. Alex Luthor was ambushed in an alley by Lex Luthor and the Joker. While Lex wanted revenge from Alex for impersonating him, the Joker was the one who was madder for being invited to the party. The Joker melted half of his face with acid and shot him in the face, ending his life.

sections.title: Booster Gold: Outshined
items: The Booster Gold Memorial was created to memorialise Booster Gold following his apparent death while containing the explosion of a nuclear submarine within Metropolis.

After going through a series of unfortunate events, including the termination of his sponsorship contract with Ferris Aircraft and losing the spotlight to the new hero, Supernova, Booster Gold asked Skeets to search history for a threat he could face to recover his reputation in Metropolis. Skeets found out that a nuclear submarine would crash in Metropolis Midtown on that very same day.

But the nuclear submarine is only part of the problem. Ballostro, a monstrous sea creature, attached itself to the ship to hunt prey on land. Booster Gold engaged him in a disastrous battle that resulted in Superman Statue losing its head, a blackout, and infrastructural damage. Soon, Supernova arrives to help. To Booster's chagrin, he gets rid of Ballostro and provides light for the people in the area. After being hostilized by the very people he was trying to save, Supernova called him "a billboard" and his heroic acts nothing but "stunts", and that was when Booster Gold finally snapped, attacking his rival. The duo threw punches and insults at each other until they were interrupted by Skeets, who warned them about the damage the creature caused to the submarine's nuclear engine, leaving it on the brink of explosion. Attempting to have all the glory to himself, Booster used the technology of his suit to engulf both him and the submarine in a force-field to contain the explosion, raising the structure high enough to avoid more damage - but the blast that followed was too powerful. Supernova caught his body before he could hit the ground, but a skeleton in a supersuit was all that remained of the disgraced hero.

A few months later, Booster Gold returned, revealing that Rip Hunter had switched him with his actual future corpse right before the explosion, placing him 12 weeks back in time so he could help Rip prepare to face a bigger threat. Supernova was him all along, a disguise that allowed him to coexist with his past-self without being detected.

sections.title: Notes
items: In each of the stories, the formation of the Justice League varies:; Death and Return of Superman: Booster Gold, Bloodwynd ( J'onn J'onzz), Blue Beetle (Ted Kord), Fire, Ice, Green Lantern Guy Gardner, Maxima are part of the Justice League America, a branch of the Justice League International based on New York.; Further adaptations of the story ( Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice, Justice League and its director's cut, as well as the The Death of Superman & Reign of the Supermen animated films) would have the actual Justice League, specifically the iteration presented in The New 52 event - but Hal Jordan would not receive the live action treatment.; JLA: New World Order: Two versions of the Justice League are present in the story. Metamorpho, Icemaiden, Nuklon, and Obsidian are part of the Justice League America, a branch of the Justice League International based on New York. The Justice League of America (JLA) is comprised by Superman, Batman, Wonder Woman, Martian Manhunter, Green Lantern Kyle Rayner, Wally West's Flash, and a reluctant Aquaman.; Superman: For Tomorrow: The Justice League present in the story is comprised by Superman, Batman, Wonder Woman, Aquaman, Martian Manhunter, Wally West's Flash, and Green Lantern John Stewart.; Infinite Crisis: Due to internal conflicts, the Justice League is disbanded at the start of this Crisis. It was comprised of Superman, Wonder Woman, Batman, Aquaman, Martian Manhunter, Wally West's Flash, Green Lantern John Stewart, Green Lantern Hal Jordan, Hawkman, Green Arrow, Black Canary, Zatanna, and Red Tornado.

sections.title: Trivia
items: JLA: New World Order; The concept of the Watchtower is introduced at the end of story as an actual tower built on the Moon's surface.; WGBS-TV is one of the media vehicles covering Hyperclan's actions on Earth.

Superman: For Tomorrow; WHAK! Cola ads can be seen in multiple settings.; The baseball game showed in the third issue is a match between the Monarchs and an unspecified team.; Metropia is a blend of the words Metropolis and utopia.
Infinite Crisis; The Watchtower introduced in New World Order is destroyed by Superboy-Prime; it was superseded by the Hall of Justice in Washington D.C. and the Satellite Watchtower.

sections.title: Trivia
items: Gotham Central was the name of a police procedural DC comic book series that ran from February 2003 to April 2006. The series focused on the Gotham City Police Department and the difficulties its officers faced living and working in Gotham City. Each of the characters mentioned in this collection is part of the series (possible spoilers ahead):

Jim Corrigan (not to be confused with the unrelated first host of the Spectre) was a corrupt detective who used to steal and sell crime scene memorabilia, and was killed by Crispus Allen's son as revenge against his father's death. He first appeared in the Gotham Central series.
Ron Probson was the commander of GCPD's Major Crimes Unit's second shift. He was created for the Gotham Central series, in which he was killed by the Joker.

Harvey Bullock is a shady police officer, ex-partner of Renee Montoya. He got kicked off the force for leading a witness protection member's identity to the mob. The mobster shot Commissioner Gordon, but got away because Harvey stole the evidence. Harvey first appeared in Detective Comics #441 (1974), and appears in the Gotham Central series.

Michael Akins (misspelled as Atkins) worked for the Gateway City Police Department before moving to Gotham City and joining the GCPD force, and became the commissioner when Gordon decided to retire after he got shot. He first appeared in Batman: Turning Points #5 (2001) and is the commissioner in the GCPD during the Gotham Central series.

Josephine Macdonald (a.k.a. Josie Mac) is a detective with minor psychic powers who was transferred to the Missing Persons Department after she discovered that the mayor's wife was cheating on him. After arresting the responsible for the kidnapping of the mob boss Anthony Antonelli's grandson, Josie was transferred to the Major Crimes Unit, filling in for Montoya for a time before becoming Marcus Driver partner on the second shift. She first appeared in Detective Comics #763 (2001), and appears in the Gotham Central series.

Crispus Allen was an agnostic police veteran born in Metropolis and transferred to Gotham, partnering with Renee Montoya in the Major Crimes Unit. He was killed by Jim Corrigan after finding about Corrigan's misconducts during the Gotham Central series, and became the Spectre second host after that. He first appeared in Detective Comics #742 (2000).

Renee Montoya was a prominent GCDP detective in the comics, until she resigned after attempting to kill Jim Corrigan as revenge for the death of her partner Crispus Allen by the end of the Gotham Central series. She was later chosen by Vic Sage as his successor and became The Question. Montoya first appeared in Batman #475 (1992).

Romy Chandler trained to become an FBI agent, but gave up on it due the amount of paperwork she had to deal with, and her skills granted her a position in the GCPD Major Crime Unit, working as a liaison between the GCPD and the FBI, and has a secretive romance with Marcus Driver. She first appeared in the Gotham Central series.
Marcus Driver is a quite heroic detective, partner of Josie Mac, and has a secretive romance with Romy Chandler. He first appeared in the Gotham Central series.

items: The collection first was introduced in 2018.

Most of the movies named in the collection are references to real-life romantic films:; "Sleepless in Star City" is a reference to " Sleepless in Seattle", and Star City where Green Arrow traditionally operates.; "(52) Day Of Summer" is a reference to " (500) Days of Summer", and 52, an important number to the DC mythos (an example being the New 52 reboot).; "The 40-Year-Old Sidekick" is a reference to " The 40-Year-Old Virgin".; "My Big Fat Atlantean Wedding" is a reference to " My Big Fat Greek Wedding". The original Atlantis, on which the Atlantis in the DC Universe is based, originates from Ancient Greek literature.; "Nth-Metal Linings Playbook" is a reference to " Silver Linings Playbook". Nth-Metal is a fictional precious metal in the DC Universe.; "How To Lose A Hero In 10 Days" is a reference to " How to Lose a Guy in 10 Days".; "Pretty Villain" is a reference to " Pretty Woman".; "Crazy, Stupid, Heroics" is a reference to " Crazy, Stupid, Love."; "The Amazonian Princess Bride" is a reference to " The Princess Bride". The "Amazonian Princess" most likely refers to Wonder Woman.; "When Barry Met Iris..." is a reference to " When Harry Met Sally".; "Save Anything" is likely a reference to " Say Anything".
The name of the feat for completing the collection is a reference to the term " Netflix and chill". The title granted may be a reference to any one of the love songs with the same name.

Batman's mail message refers the Earth 3 episode, and the movie "The Three Racketeers" is probably the one he watched as it's the only one Catwoman never saw, because it literally does not exist on the regular Earth. It is a reference to the novel The Three Musketeers, which has been adapted to film numerous times.

sections.title: Trivia
items: The locations appear to be based on The Daily Planet Guide to Gotham City, part of a series of supplements for the DC Universe Roleplaying Game. The following quotes are from the Guide:

Majestic Theater (p. 107-108): " The grand old movie house of the city, the Majestic was recently rebuilt to its original 1920s glory thanks to a generous grant from the Wayne Foundation. At the same time the theater restored its fixtures and appearance and updated its technology for showing films. It can now show regular as well as digital films. The theater's facade and lobby will be of interest to history buffs, as they incorporate three different types of marble quarried from three regions of Italy, a practice common in the Gilded Age and lovingly reproduced as part of the theaters recent overhaul." It is also referred to as "Majestic Theatre" and appear sporadically in the comics.

Kane Art Museum (p. 105): " Collecting the finest contemporary art, the Kane Museum features few permanent exhibits, choosing instead to showcase current trends in advertising, conceptual, commercial, and performance art. Visitors can wander from room to room in the Kane viewing, for example, barbarians painted on oil by a fantasist, then computer-generated billboard copy, followed by a collection of political cartoons. This museum is a required experience for those wanting to remain current in the world of art. Supported by a grant from Alan Scott." The museum appears in Detective Comics #664 (1993) during the Batman: Knightfall event.

Gotham Zoo (p. 104): " Once again a going concern following No Man's Land, the Gotham Zoo has consolidated its exhibits in its northern Coventry location due to the closure of its Robinson Park facility. Since the completion of the move, the zoo seeks to regain its reputation among the best zoos for cities the size of Gotham. Well known for its penguin habitat, as well as the African savanna environment that recaptures the beauty and majesty of the African veld, the Gotham Zoo is a favorite destination for springtime field trips and summertime day trips for many residents of the city and surrounding area." The zoo first appear in Batman #19 (1943).

Arkham Asylum (p. 134-135): " Arkham Asylum on Mercey Island [colloquially known as Arkham Island] , administered by Dr. Jeremiah Arkham, remains our primary holding center for those felons considered both highly dangerous to the public and too mentally ill for the regular prison system. Founded in 1921 as the Elizabeth Arkham Asylum for the Criminally Insane by Dr. Amadeus Arkham and originally based in Sommerset, this legendary facility has undergone several renovations and one physical change of address in the last 80 years. Security measures are being considerably updated at the joint expense of the city, state, and federal governments. The new systems are expected to be fully operational by September of this year. One major change is in effect, however: the Joker is no longer being held at Arkham. Following his recent rampage as Quraci ambassador to the United Nations [as seen in Batman: A Death in the Family, except the country was Iran instead of Qurac] , he has been remanded to the indefinite custody of Slabside Island on grounds of federal jurisdiction over his latest offences." The Asylum first appeared in Batman #258 (1974).

Luigi's Pizza (p. 91): " Another Gotham entrepreneurial success story, the first Luigi's was opened almost 20 years ago near what is now called Little Odessa. Fighting off nationally known competitors, Luigi's has expanded and now has over 80 delivery stations and 14 family-style sit-down pizzerias located throughout the city and surrounding areas. There's rarely a weekend night in the city where a Luigi's delivery station isn't apologizing because of the 45-minute delivery time due to their fully packed delivery schedule. But as Luigi himself says on the commercial, "Itsa worth the wait!"" Luigi first appeared in Action Comics #419 (1972), and was created for the Human Target series.

Planet Krypton-Gotham (p. 89): " The latest entry of the growing chain of hero-themed restaurants, Planet Krypton-Gotham made its debut within the Crystal Palace/America's Mall complex shortly after it opened. Its gala opening was attended by the likes of Booster Gold, Blue Beetle [likely Ted Kord] , and Firehawk, as seen on the WGBS's coverage of the event. Similar to the other Planet Kryptons, the Gotham City version features themed decorations that celebrate the presence of super heroes in our world, such as replicas of Hawkman's helmet and a copy of the original charter of the Justice Society of America, signed by FDR. In keeping with the tradition of styling the restaurant to its location, Planet Krypton has a substantial Justice Society dining area and several darker areas with artistic interpretations of the Batman and other super heroes rumored to operate within the confines of Gotham City. As with the rest of the chain, servers are dressed as members of the Justice League. They serve topical meals, such as the Aquamanwich (a large fish sandwich with a harpoon holding it together), the Man of Beef and Supershake combo meal, and the Greens Lantern (a salad that comes with Planet Krypton's signature avocado dressing). Like its sister restaurants, Planet Krypton has dozens of video monitors that display coverage of super-hero events around the globe, as well as Planet Krypton's exclusive JLA Mooncam—a camera directed at the JLA Watchtower on the moon when it is in phase." The original Planet Krypton restaurant is located in Metropolis, owned and operated by Booster Gold, first appearing in Kingdom Come #1 (1996).

sections.title: Trivia (continued 2)
items: Iceberg Lounge (p. 86-87): " Owned and operated by Oswald Cobblepot—the individual who had formerly gone by the moniker of "The Penguin"—the Iceberg has become one of the hottest nightspots in the city and on the entire East Coast, perhaps due to the notoriety of the owner. Constantly the site of movie premiere parties and political $1,000-a-plate fund-raisers, the Iceberg's namesake is a large, central, chilled, lagoon filled with miniature icebergs and featuring live penguins. Have no fear though; the lagoon is cordoned off with the latest technology that keeps the penguins, their aroma, and the cold air inside well enclosed, while a comfortable temperature is maintained within the rest of the restaurant. Naturally known for its seafood, the Iceberg has earned a four-star rating on numerous critics' lists. It is also praised for its nightly entertainment, featuring jazz and world-famous vocalists. Many an unknown has stood in front of the Iceberg backdrop one night and signed a multi-record deal the next. Not a family-style restaurant per se, the Iceberg is open for dinner and late night. Private dining rooms are made available at the discretion of the management." The Lounge first appeared in Detective Comics #683 (1995).

Amusement Mile (p. 109-110): " Gotham's permanent amusement park was first built in the 1930s as a Depression Era project. While the Mile saw ups and down in popularity, it's currently experiencing a resurgence in interest and funding following No Man's Land. By opening its gates free to different Gotham neighborhoods on weekday evenings as part of the celebration following Gotham City's re-opening, the Mile has greatly helped its image. The amusement park features Ferris wheels, miniature roller coasters, and other thrill rides, as well as games of chance and shows. Its eastern end is where many circuses set up during their stay in Gotham." The Mile, inspired by Coney Island, first appeared in Batman #569 (1999).

sections.title: Trivia
items: About the locations mentioned:

Aparo Expressway is the eastern expressway that connects the R.H. Kane Building to One Gotham Center in DCUO. The version in the comics is much larger, and connects Port Adams in the southern island to the northern island.
Novick Tunnel is one of the many submerged tunnels connecting the western part of the islands to the mainland. It was named after the comic book artist Irv Novick.

Peckinpah Street intersects with Saint Street, and the Noonan's Bar (first appeared in The Demon Annual Vol 3 #2 in 1993) is located on the corner of the two. It's named after the director Sam Peckinpah.
Broome Street intersects with Finger Street, and the Wayne Tower (first appeared in Batman: Legends of the Dark Knight #27 in 1992) is located on the corner of the two.
Sprang Bridge is the bridge that connects the Burnley Freight Yards with the southern part of the Burnley district. It is where the Sprang Bridge Soldiers used to operate.
Westward Bridge is the bridge connects Arkham Island to the Otisburg district.
Park Row became known as Crime Alley after billionaires Thomas and Martha Wayne were murdered there in front of their son, Bruce Wayne.
Saint Street intersects with Peckinpah Street, and the Noonan's Bar (first appeared in The Demon Annual Vol 3 #2 in 1993) is located on the corner of the two.

sections.title: Trivia
items: The following characters are mentioned in the list:; Two-Face refers to Harvey Dent's evil alter ego (whose name is in the Holiday Nice List). This might be a reference to the villain version of the events of Old Gotham Subway (in the comics, Two-Face is not featured in any significant Christmas-themed story).; Lex Luthor is present many Christmas-themed stories, but the one that is most pertinent to game's story is The Most Wonderful Time of the Year, published in 52 #33 (2006).; Noah Kuttler is the civilian identity of Calculator. He is probably listed here for assisting new villains during the Winter Holidays.; Oswald Chesterfield Cobblepot is the civilian identity of the Penguin. Cobblepot stands out in two Christmas-related stories. One of them is The Penguin's Apprentice, an earlier story first published in Batman #27 (1940); the other is the movie Batman Returns, released in 1992 as a sequel to Batman (1989).; Thaddeus Bodog Sivana is the full name of Doctor Sivana, one of Shazam's main villains. He's named here as a possible reference to the story The Year Without a Christmas! by E. Nelson Bridwell, Bob Oksner, and Vince Colletta, first published in Shazam! #11 (1973).; Lobo crossed out his name and carved Easter Bunny's name instead - a reference to the story Lobo Paramilitary Christmas Special by Keith Giffen, Alan Grant, and Simon Bisley. It was first published in 1992.

summary: It's a Horrible Life is a collection of twelve items related to timeline changes and The Flash. These can be obtained directly from Flashpoint Time Capsules.

sections.title: Collectibles
items: " Attempting to change fate has effects that ripple out backwards and forwards in time, touching everyone and everything in this Flashpoint."

sections.title: Mail Messages
items: Upon completion of this collection players receive a message from Reverse Flash or The Flash, accessible from any Mail Terminal.
Heroes:
Villains:

table.caption: Mail Messages
rows: " You have to be able to see all of this and finally objectively agree that Flash is selfish, reckless and self-centered. This is proof that he wasn't even able to learn his lesson when the world was on the line. He got into this mess because he couldn't see beyond the consequences of his actions. Then he almost lost everything helping a cause in a timeline that shouldn't even exist. No vision, no forethought, and no guts. I trust his guilt is self-evident."

table.caption: Mail Messages
rows: " That Reverse-Flash guy was so focused on trying to humiliate me personally that he refused to set aside our differences even to save the Earth from total destruction! I mean, all of Europe sunk! Lots of people got stabbed by Amazons (and stabs hurt)! And it wasn't even like Thawne had an escape plan; he knew that he was going to die alongside everyone else. Even though you and I don't see eye-to-eye, I'm glad you're not so obsessed that you'd let everyone on Earth get drown-stab-'sploded just to spite me. So, thanks, I guess?"

sections.title: Trivia
items: The effects of these various specimen are as follows:; Black Kryptonite: Can divide a Kryptonian into two people, with one exhibiting their "dark" personality traits.; Blue Kryptonite: Can affect Bizarros much like Green Kryptonite can affect Kryptonians. Can also cause Bizarros to speak clearly, think rationally and be exceedingly polite.; Gold Kryptonite: Can alter a Kryptonian's physiology, destroying the ability of Kryptonian cells to process solar energy and robbing them of their super-abilities for fifteen seconds.; Green Kryptonite: Toxic to Kryptonians. Can be used to counter the effects of any other form of Kryptonite that may enter a Kryptonian's system.; Orange Kryptonite: Can bestow kryptonian powers onto animals for twenty-four hours.; Phantom Zone Kryptonite: Also known as Jewel Kryptonite. Can amplify the psychic powers of Phantom Zone residents, allowing them to project illusions into the "real world" or perform mind control. It was made from what was left of a mountain range on Krypton called the Jewel Mountains.; Red Kryptonite: Brings out the rebellious and immoral personality of Kryptonians and rids them of their inhibitions.; White Kryptonite: Toxic to plant life.

sections.title: Trivia
items: All of the components are types of rocks:
Anorthosite is a phaneritic, intrusive igneous rock, and can be found in the light-coloured areas of the Moon's surface. I can also be found in e Earth and Mars.
Pyroxene is a group of rock-forming inosilicate minerals found in many igneous and metamorphic rocks. It's the most abundant dark mineral on the Moon's surface.
Ilmenite is a titanium-iron oxide mineral. It is the main source of titanium dioxide, which is used in paints, printing inks, fabrics, plastics, paper, sunscreen, food and cosmetics.
Norite is a mafic intrusive igneous rock composed of the calcium-rich plagioclase labradorite, orthopyroxene, and olivine. It is a common rock type of the Apollo samples.
Troctolite is a mafic intrusive rock type. It consists essentially of variable amounts of olivine and calcic plagioclase along with minor pyroxene.
Olivine is a magnesium iron silicate. It has many uses, such as the green gemstone peridot, as well as industrial applications like metalworking processes.

sections.title: Trivia
items: These cards of fortune are based on the Major Arcana, a set of 22 tarot cards. It tells the story "The Fool's Journey", starting with "The Fool Card" and ending in the "The World Card".
There's no actual tarot card named "Sickness".
Each peace of the collection possibly refers to one of the major characters in the episode.

In tarot, each of the cards have the following meaning:; The Death Card: when upright, it might indicate the end of a cycle, new beginnings, change, or transformation; when reversed, it might indicate fear of change, holding on, stagnation, decay.; The Magician Card: when upright, it might indicate willpower, desire, creation, manifestation; when reversed, it might indicate trickery, illusions, out of touch.; The Judgement Card: when upright, it might indicate reflection, reckoning, awakening; when reversed, it might indicate lack of self awareness, doubt, self loathing.; The Fool Card: when upright, it might indicate innocence, new beginnings, free spirit; when reversed, it might indicate recklessness, taken advantage of, inconsideration.; The Hanged Card: when upright, it might indicate sacrifice, release, martyrdom; when reversed, it might indicate stalling, needless sacrifice, fear of sacrifice.; The Tower Card: when upright, it might indicate sudden upheaval, broken pride, disaster; when reversed, it might indicate disaster avoided, delayed disaster, fear of suffering.; The Moon Card: when upright, it might indicate unconscious, illusions, intuition; when reversed, it might indicate confusion, fear, misinterpretation.; The Sun Card: when upright, it might indicate joy, success, celebration, positivity; when reversed, it might indicate negativity, depression, sadness.; The World Card: when upright, it might indicate fulfillment, harmony, completion; when reversed, it might indicate incompletion, no closure.; The Hermit Card: when upright, it might indicate contemplation, search for truth, inner guidance; when reversed, it might indicate loneliness, isolation, lost the way.; The Chariot Card : when upright, it might indicate direction, control, willpower; when reversed, it might indicate lack of control, lack of direction, aggression.
The other tarot cards are: The Hight Priestess, The Empress, The Emperor, The Hierophant, The Lovers, Strength, The Wheel of Fortune, Justice, Temperance, The Devil, and The Star.

sections.title: Trivia
items: The locations appear to be based on The Daily Planet Guide to Metropolis, part of a series of supplements for the DC Universe Roleplaying Game. The following quotes are from the Guide:

S.T.A.R. Labs (p. 66-67): " S.T.A.R. Labs is another major player in the city’s technology scene, providing jobs for over a thousand residents in its main Queensland Park laboratory facility, offices downtown, and in Secord Park. While S.T.A.R. Labs does not manufacture any of the technology it creates or refines, it does sell licenses to other companies, who then may produce items utilizing the technology. Given its pure research approach to science and technology as well as its dependence on license fees for its operating budget, S.T.A.R. Labs is one of Metropolis’s most security conscious businesses, often requiring a four-day waiting period to acquire a visitor’s pass. Due to an explosion at S.T.A.R. Labs’s downtown facility three years ago that threatened to cause a meltdown in the facility’s nuclear generator, the city council passed a law requiring all businesses in the borough of New Troy to be powered by city electricity or solar power. Unable to meet its energy needs with either option, S.T.A.R. Labs moved to its current location in Queensland Park. Here it is a focal point for several smaller technology start-ups, which have formed a technology/industrial park around the S.T.A.R. Labs complex." It first appeared in Superman #246 (1971).

Stryker’s Island (p. 128): " Located in the East River midway between New Troy [the main Metropolis island in DCUO] and Queensland Park is Stryker’s Island Maximum Security Correctional Facility, one of the toughest prisons in the nation. While the original buildings on Stryker’s date back to just after the Civil War, the island has been used to house Metropolis’ reprobates for at least 200 years. [...] Since its founding, Stryker’s has been home to tens of thousands of criminals, from the tamest (such as Edward Robinson, who broke into homes of single women to steal their shoes and had amassed over 20,000 pairs by the time he was caught) to the infamous (such as Bloodsport and other powerful but non-metahuman criminals) that are apprehended in Metropolis. The prison, like many in United States, is continually overcrowded, often with four prisoners sharing a room designed for two men." It first appeared in Superman Vol 2 #9 (198787

Big Belly Burger (p. 83): " Another chain that started right here in Metropolis, Big Belly is, right beside Superman, the pride of the city, with enough loyal patrons year in and year out to keep competition limited. Chef Mike, the owner of the chain, still works at the downtown Big Belly, located just one block east from the Daily Planet. Most days, you can catch Planet columnists and staffers grabbing a quick lunch." It first appeared in Adventures of Superman #441 (1988).

LexCorp Building (p. 25-26): " Founding his own company, LexCorp, in a two-office suite in the top floor of the Daily Planet building, Luthor didn’t have to wait long to hear from the Department of Defense, awarding LexCorp a $6 billion contract for 18 LexWings as well as his consultation on revitalizing the United States Air Force. With this financial security, Luthor first addressed Metropolis from the steps of City Hall, telling the assembled masses that he would never allow any of the contract money to leave Metropolis—all work, from construction to development of new technologies for new aircraft would be performed within the city’s borders. The announcement was just what the ailing city needed. With the prospects of high-tech jobs, enrollment in all of Metropolis’s colleges and universities skyrocketed, and smaller businesses were once again attracted to the city, eager to be part of Luthor’s success, or hoping, like S.T.A.R. Labs, to attract skilled high-tech workers to their own facilities. Shortly thereafter, Luthor himself, only 23, broke ground for the 96-story LexCorp Tower near the old Shuster Customs House, shaped in a characteristic “L.”" According to Who's Who in the DC Universe #11, it first appeared in The Man of Steel #2 (1986).

Daily Planet (p. 73-74): " Print communication had its advent in Metropolis early on with the Daily Planet and, later, the Daily Star. While the Daily Planet has grown in the ensuing years to become a major newspaper with a global audience and circulation, the Daily Star has remained a smaller paper [...]. [...] Of the newspapers within the city, only the Daily Planet can boast of never missing a single issue since its start on January 1, 1793. Even when the city was destroyed during the Fall of Metropolis , the newspaper was able to publish thanks to its backup presses located in Queensland Park. The Planet's record was broken early last year when the newspaper was bought and dismantled by Lex Luthor in an attempt to consolidate his media holdings. Although the Planet languished for six months, it was eventually restarted when Luthor, convinced he had made a bad investment, sold the newspaper to former editor-turned-publisher Perry White. Since its presses have started up again, the Planet is as proud a publication as ever. It continues to publish timely and well-researched articles, in keeping with its enduring tradition of quality journalism." It first appeared in Action Comics #23 (1940).

sections.title: Trivia (continued 2)
items: Planet Krypton (p. 88-89): " Planet Krypton is by far, the coolest eating house this side of Mars for those into the hero-watching game. While Planet Kryptons have been popping up all around the country, Metropolis’s is the first and, by all accounts, still the best. For the newcomer, plan to spend at least three hours plus the time you spend eating. The interior of the restaurant houses the most complete collection of super-hero and villain replicas ever assembled, including Batman’s Batarangs, Hawkman’s visor, and a wide array of weapons from super villains of all styles and shapes. Be warned before you go—the Planet Krypton experience is heavily hero oriented, from waiters dressed as members of the Justice League to themed meals such as the Big Barda Burger, the Man of Beef and Supershake combo meal, and the Titano Tower (a six-inch high sandwich with world-famous banana spread). Servings of all entrees come available in three sizes: Atom (for kids), Teen Titanic (for medium appetites) and Super (for big eaters). Planet Krypton is also the exclusive distributor of Lobobrew Beer, micro-brewed on the premises and based on a recipe from on the abrasive alien known only as Lobo. While the restaurant was recently damaged when the Challengers of the Unknown accidentally made it their landing pad, renovations have been completed and Planet Krypton is looking better than ever! Be sure to check out the 53 separate video monitors that automatically tune to hero coverage around the globe, as well as Planet Krypton’s exclusive JLA Mooncam—a camera aimed at the JLA Watchtower on the moon when it is in phase." It first appeared in Kingdom Come #1 (1996).

Cain Theatre (p. 101): " Named after Robert Cain, the leading man of hundreds of plays and musicals in the 1930s, the Cain Theatre is best known today for its traditional 1930s look and rumors of two ghosts—a tall, thin man and a shorter fat man—that supposedly haunt the orchestra pit. The Cain is a stop for many Broadway touring shows."

Ace O’ Clubs (p. 82): " One of Metropolis’s most colorful establishments with one of Metropolis’s most colorful residents as its owner. The Ace O’ Clubs is one of Superman’s favorite eating places—just ask the owner, Bibbo, Superman’s biggest fan." It first appeared in Adventures of Superman #428 (1987).

sections.title: Trivia
items: About the streets mentioned:
1938 Sullivan Lane (New Troy island) is where Clark Kent and Lois Lane's apartment building is located, a wedding present from Bruce Wayne. It first appeared in Superman: The Wedding Album #1 (1996).
344 Clinton Street is a high-rise apartment complex where Superman lived for the most part of his superhero career. It first appeared in Superman #46 (1947).

Bessolo Boulevard is named after George Reeves (his real name being George Bessolo), the first actor to play Superman in a feature film, and it's the Metropolis' version of Broadway (NY). One of its earliest appearances is in Adventures of Superman #488 (1992).
Topaz Lane is another Metropolis' version of Broadway, located in the New Troy island.
Collyer Street is named after actor Bud Collyer, who voiced Superman in the first adaptation of the character — The Adventures of Superman, a radio show.
Coates Boulevard is named after Phyllis Coates, the first actress to play Lois Lane in a feature film.
Riddler's mail connects this collection to the Gotham's Gang War story arc.

sections.title: Trivia
items: No Man's Land was a Bat Family crossover event. In the story, a magnitude 7.6 earthquake had devastated Gotham City, killing thousands. In an effort to rehabilitate the city, the government of the United States declared it a no man's land, forcing the island into a quarantine - including the destruction of the bridges connecting it to the mainland - with every entrance guarded by the U.S. Army. Anarchy followed, with Arkham Asylum former inmates and gangs fighting for control - Penguin, Bane (working for Lex Luthor), Scarecrow, Two-Face, Mister Freeze, Joker and Clayface amongst them. Batman, Oracle, Huntress, and Batgirl, as well as some officers from GCPD ( James Gordon included) decided to stay in the city to fight, while the Justice League prevented the invasion of outside forces ( Poison Ivy negotiated a truce with Batman in exchange of providing produce from time to time). The constant territorial disputes made so that the territory contested by each faction would constantly change.; The Gotham City map presented in this event became canonical in the DC Universe, and it is also the base for Gotham in DC Universe Online.

sections.title: Trivia
items: Originally this was one of the most difficult collections to gather in the whole game since merely one spawn point on the whole of Arkham Island was active at a time, the respawn rate was very low and additionally this was shared with the other two collections which can exclusively be found there.

The phobias mentioned in this collection mean the following:; Ornithophobia is the fear of birds; Coulrophobia is the fear of clowns; Technophobia is the fear of new technology; Frigophobia is the fear of cold; Brontophobia is the fear of thunder or lightning; Aerophobia is the fear of flying; Hemophobia is the fear of blood; Xanthophobia is the fear of the color yellow; Triskaidekaphobia is the fear of the number 13; Chiroptophobia is the fear of bats

Each phobia may refer to one or more iconic characters:; Ornithophobia may refer to either Black Canary, Penguin, Robin, Hawkman, Hawkgirl or the Birds of Prey; Coulrophobia may refer to either Joker or Harley Quinn — and both ex-Robin Red Hood and Oracle have motives to fear the Clown Prince of Crime; Technophobia may refer to Brainiac, Metallo, Hank Henshaw, or Cyborg; Frigophobia may refer to Mister Freeze, Captain Cold, Killer Frost, Ice, or even Superman, Supergirl, Power Girl, or Bizarro; Brontophobia may refer to Black Lightning, Static, Shazam, Black Adam, The Flash, Professor Zoom, or Weather Wizard; Aerophobia may refer all iconics that are able to fly, but may also refer to Nightwing, whose family was known as The Flying Graysons; Hemophobia may refer to Jason Blood or Brother Blood; Xanthophobia may refer to the Sinestro Corps, or Professor Zoom; Triskaidekaphobia may refer to Doctor Thirteen; Chiroptophobia may refer to Batman (who has chiroptophobia), Batgirl, or Batwoman.

sections.title: Trivia
items: The plaques memorialize various events that have occurred previous in the DC Universe.; The Amazons Attack Plaque was created to memorialize an incident where the Amazons of Themyscira staged an attack on the United States of America following political bullying by the country and the illegal imprisonment of their princess, Wonder Woman.; The War Games Plaque was created to memorialise a three day, city-wide gang war that erupted between all of Gotham City's criminal groups.; The No Man's Land Plaque was created to memorialize a time when Gotham City, following an earthquake that destroyed the entire city, was abandoned by the United States Government.; The Rann-Thanagarian War Plaque was created to memorialize the galactic territorial war between Rann and Thanagar that was instigated by Superboy-Prime and Alexander Luthor during the Infinite Crisis.; The Day of Vengeance Plaque was created to memorialize the victims of the Spectre's rampage across Earth during the Infinite Crisis.

sections.title: Mail Messages
items: Upon completion of this collection players receive a message from Supergirl or Metallo, accessible from any Mail Terminal.

Villains:

table.caption: Mail Messages
rows: " When tragedy occurs, it's always tempting to give in to anger and take it out on someone, anyone to blame. But as heroes, we have to always remember: what if that person was framed, or being controlled, or an evil clone? Or what if you're just mistaken? It happens a lot, in superhero circles. It's because it's so hard to accept that not everything's conspiracy, some things are just random, terrible events. You have to be prepared for that, too. I appreciate that you help me be prepared for anything. Take this, to remember that by."

table.caption: Mail Messages
rows: " This is the scarf of the killer of Krypton himself, Rogol Zaar. And now it's yours to wear proudly. Wear it when you see Superman. Wear it when you see Supergirl. Wear it when you see that ridiculous mutt, Krypto. Never let them forget that they come from a planet that was so universaly hated that nobody in the multiverse shed a single tear when it went up in smoke."

It is one of three Collections that comprise the Treasures of the Vanguard metacollection.

table.caption: Mail Messages
rows: " The realm of magic is full of mysteries of the most peculiar kind. These runes you've collected will distract me with a few moments of interest and provide clues about their owners. Thanks, associate."

sections.title: Item
items: This collection rewards the player with the Belt of the Archmagus waist item (style: Wizardly).

sections.title: Trivia
items: Each of the runes belongs to a magical faction featured in the classic game.
The Magents of Chaos are the minions of Felix Faust. They can be found in Metropolis Chinatown and at Gotham University Campus.
The Amazons of Themyscira are the forces led by Wonder Woman. They can be found in Metropolis' Tomorrow District.
The Cult of Blood are the minions of Brother Blood. They can be found in Metropolis Chinatown and at Gotham's Robinson Park.
The Cult of Trigon are the demons that embody the seven deadly sins. They can be found in Metropolis' Chinatown and Tomorrow District, as well as Gotham's Robinson Park.
The Atlanteans are the forces led by Aquaman. They can be found in Metropolis' Suicide Slums.
The Bestiamorph Army the minions Circe. They can be found in Metropolis' Chinatown and Tomorrow District.
The Sentinels of Magic are the forces led by Doctor Fate. They can be found in Metropolis' Chinatown and Midtown, as well as Gotham's Robinson Park.

sections.title: Collectibles
items: " Possible figures in the Source Wall."

sections.title: Mail Messages
items: Upon completion of this collection players receive a message from Oracle or Calculator, accessible from any Mail Terminal.
Heroes
Villains

table.caption: Mail Messages
rows: " I'm a little confused by some of the people you say you spotted in the Source Wall, but it's still an interesting list! Thanks for putting this together. If... I mean... when, this whole Multiverse apocalypse thing gets sorted out, I'd be surprised if they stayed stuck in the Wall or whether they got free. I hope we get the chance to find out together!"

table.caption: Mail Messages
rows: " Look, I'm not calling you a liar or anything, but this list of people you say you spotted in the Source Wall? Kinda fishy. Even if it is real, which I seriously doubt, no way they stay stuck in the Wall once we sort out this whole Multiverse apocalypse thing. Still, intel is intel, and I always pay out."

sections.title: Item
items: This collection rewards the player with the Connective Energy catalyst.

sections.title: Trivia
items: As the mail messages indicate, this is indeed an odd list:; Ares, Darkseid, Anti-Monitor, and Orion are characters who have appeared in the game. They are all supposed to be active, except Darkseid who was seemingly destroyed in Wonderverse: Fractured God Sphere and Grail is looking for him in Dark Knights: New Apokolips.; Superboy-Prime, Relic, and Yuga Khan are established DC characters who have yet to appear in-game.; Liga, European Dictator, and World-Eater don't directly correspond to any known DC character. "Liga" is Polish for "League". "European Dictator" is likely a way to refer to Marvel's Doctor Doom without mentioning him by name, as Doom was shown imprisoned in the Source Wall in JLA/Avengers. Likewise World-Eater is likely a reference to Galactus, who was shown imprisoned in the wall as an easter egg during Justice League Unlimited.
Ares, Darkseid, and Anti-Monitor trapped in the Source Wall are available as base items in the 2023 Attack of the Anti-Monitor event.

sections.title: Trivia
items: WayneTech is the tech branch of Wayne Enterprises. It's owned by billionaire Bruce Wayne (a.k.a. Batman) and commanded by Lucius Fox, and first appeared in The Brave and the Bold #113 (1974).
The Fear Gas is Scarecrow's Fear Toxin. It first appeared in Batman #189 (1967).

Mobster Stealth Circuitry is a possible reference to the mobster "Matches" Malone - he was a mobster whose identity was taken by Bruce Wayne after Malone's death. The real Malone first appeared in Batman #242 (1972), while Batman's alter ego first appeared in Batman #588 (2001).
The SCU is the GCPD Special Crimes Unit.
Venom is a highly addictive super-steroid, commonly associated with Bane, who's is both a user and a trafficker. It first appeared in Batman: Legends of the Dark Knight #16 (1991).
The OMACs are nanotechnologically enhanced cyborgs controlled by Brother Eye, programmed to annihilate super-powered beings. They first appeared in OMAC Project #1 (2005).
Jokerbot Circuitry probably refers to The Joker's Jokandroids, miniature joker-lookalike robots in DC Universe Online.

Streaky first appears in Tiny Titans during the last story in Tiny Titans #6 (2008). His official debut in the comics was in Action Comics #261 (1960).
Spot, The Atom's dog, first appears during an untitled story in Tiny Titans #9 (2008).
Bat-Cow first appeared during the story "Battle for the Cow" ( Tiny Titans #17, 2009), and made her debut in the official DC Universe in Batman Incorporated Vol 2 #1 (2012).
Blue Beetle's Bug Farm first appears during the last story in Tiny Titans #6.
Hoppy, Shazamily's rabbit, first appears in Tiny Titans in Tiny Titans #15 (2009). His official debut in the comics was in Fawcett's Funny Animals #1 (1942).
Beast Boy's Chameleon first appears during the last story in Tiny Titans #6.
Raven's Corvid Parade first appears in the story "Robin and the Robins" ( Tiny Titans #4, 2008).

Silky first appeared Tiny Titans #21 (2009). He was created for the Teen Titans animated series in 2004, and his official debut (with appearance and name as portrayed in DCUO) in the comics was in Starfire Vol 2 #9 (2016).
F.E.L.I.X. and M.A.X., Cyborg's robot pets, first appear in Tiny Titans #21.
Aqualad in Tiny Titans is Garth (a.k.a. Tempest) instead of Jackson Hyde, his successor. His fishbowl first appears during the last story in Tiny Titans #6.

Villains

table.caption: Mail Messages
rows: " I just can't believe that the world where these two get together spells such destruction for the Earth? They're both such principled and upstanding people. I know this has to trace back to someone pulling their strings. The Wonder Woman and Aquaman had to have been led astray. And I can't overlook whose fault this all is. Thank you for helping me see the damage this has all caused."

table.caption: Mail Messages
rows: " Who would have thought those two getting together would speil the absolute destruction of the Earth? I guess that's just what happens when two super-power warrior nations try to merge cultures. Well, and I'm sure the plotting advisors didn't help Queen Diana and Emperor Aquaman any. You and I, we wouldn't trust advisors like that. We know better. Here, delight in the misery alongside me!"

sections.title: Trivia
items: In the original comics and the film adaptation, Flashpoint Aquaman was married to Flashpoint Mera, but the latter was murdered by Flashpoint Wonder Woman which triggered the war between Atlanteans and Amazons. In DC Universe Online, Flashpoint Mera was killed after the war broke out, when attempting to infiltrate Themyscira (as learned in FP: The Royal War) so it is unknown what caused the fallout between Flashpoint Aquaman and Wonder Woman.

sections.title: Trivia
items: Who is the Batman? is a possible reference to the events of Frank Miller's Batman: Year One (1987). It is Batman's official origin story.

Fear of Scarecrow Grips City is a possible reference to the events of "The God of Fear" storyline in the comics ( Batman: Shadow of the Bat #16, #17, and #18, 1993), part of the Batman: Knightfall event.

Joker has escaped Arkham Asylum multiple times, but one of his most famous escapes was at the beginning of the Batman: A Death in the Family storyline (1988-1989), in which he assassinates Jason Todd with a crowbar.
No-Man's Land Ended! is a reference to the end of the No Man's Land Bat Family event (see Collections: No Man's Land for more details).
Lieutenant James Gordon was named Commissioner after the events of Batman: The Long Halloween (1996-1997) and before its sequel, Batman: Dark Victory (1999-2000).

sections.title: Trivia
items: The various items hail from various continuities starring Wonder Woman or related versions.; Fun Clinic Equipment hails from the first Wonder Woman comics, written by her creator William Moulton Marston (now part of the Earth-Two continuity). The Fun Clinic appeared in Sensation Comics #27 (1944) as a rehabilitation gym, funded by Gay Frollik, a young woman Wonder Woman rescues from attempting suicide.; Yankee Poodle’s Stars and Stripes hails from Earth-C a.k.a. Earth 26, home of Captain Carrot and the Zoo Crew. Yankee Poodle and the Zoo Crew first appeared in the story "This Bunny Unbound!" in New Teen Titans #16 (1982).; Super Hero High Letter-Woman Jacket hails from the DC Super Hero Girls 2019 animated series (a.k.a Earth 96) which portrayed Wonder Woman and other heroes as high school students in a school for heroics.; Wonder Tots’s Blankie hails from Earth-124.1. Wonder Tot is Diana as a toddler, first appearing in Wonder Woman #124 (1961).; IRAC's Interface hails from the classic Wonder Woman (1975-1979) TV series. The Information Retrieval Associative Computer, or IRAC, is an advanced A.I. computer featured in various episodes.; Dead Earth Utility Belt hails from the mini-series Wonder Woman: Dead Earth (2020) which saw Diana as one of the last people on Earth.; Made-into-Clay Bizarra "Statue" hails from the All-Star Superman continuity (2006—2008). In the limited series, she was a baby which was turned into a clay statue.; Copy of Batman’s Blues hails from the DC Animated Universe, specifically the Justice League Unlimited episode “ This Little Piggy” (2004), in which Circe turned Diana into a pig and, to restore her to normal, Batman had to sing the blues, moving the sorceress to tears.; No Man's Land Shell Fragments hails from the Wonder Woman 2017 movie, part of the DC Extended Universe. It references the scene in which Diana decides to go out of the trenches and face the German soldiers, which leads to the liberation of an occupied village.

title: Court of Aquaman (Briefings)
summary: Court of Aquaman is a briefing that can be found in the Central City Starro Deluge Zone open world zone, the Starro: The Threat Below and Starro: Spindrift Station raids of the Deluge epsiode. There are 7 parts to this briefing.

sections.title: Overview
items: Court of Aquaman is a briefing that can be found in the Central City Starro Deluge Zone open world zone, the Starro: The Threat Below and Starro: Spindrift Station raids of the Deluge epsiode. There are 7 parts to this briefing.

sections.title: Synopsis
items: "A taste of turmoil engrained in Court of Atlantis."

sections.title: Part 1: Hope of Spindrift
items: Zone: Central City Starro Deluge Zone
Location:

Briefing: Aquaman:" I am beset by opposition in my attempts to establish peace with the surface world. Resistance and resentment rain down on me from above and below the waves. The further I strive for peace, the more my image is painted as a tyrant. Despite all this, with Mera's help I have built Spindrift Station as a bridge between the land and sea, open to all who are willing. I just hope the old saying still holds true, that if you build it they will come."

images.label: Court of Aquaman - Hope of Spindrift

sections.title: Part 2: Diplomacy
items: Zone: Central City Starro Deluge Zone
Location:

Briefing: Aquaman:" The surface world's rulers view me as despot seeking to invade their countries. My attempts at diplomacy are met with criticism and insults. Is it any wonder Mera has so much vitriol for her role as "Aquawoman"? Still we have built a meeting place for the willing in Spindrift Station."

sections.title: Part 3: An Outsider
items: Zone: Atlantean Research Outpost
Instance: Starro: The Threat Below
Location:

Briefing: Aquaman:" Despite all my heroic efforts to protect the surface realm, my companions in the Justice League still only half heartedly defend my character to the press. In my court in Atlantis, my most trusted advisors question my actions and motivations down to the worthiness of my choice in a Queen. The most cowardly speak in whispers behind my back wondering if they have the spine to bring thoughts to words."

sections.title: Part 4: Doubts of a King
items: Zone: Atlantean Research Outpost
Instance: Starro: The Threat Below
Location:

Briefing: Aquaman:" Why do you curse me, Poseidon? Is it not enough that even my own wife now questions my choice to make peace? Could there be a worse time for the Conqueror of Worlds, Starro to attack the surface? How could such a thing happen not once but twice in two short years? I took every precaution. So how could Starro return once again unless someone plots against me!? Forget that I asked, since when has a King ever had need of a god."

images.label: Court of Aquaman - Doubts of a King

sections.title: Part 5: Of Two Worlds
items: Zone: Central City Starro Deluge Zone
Location:

Briefing: Mera:" Arthur is a man of two worlds, worthy of a kingdom in either. He is noble not by birth but by nature. His love and desire to have both of his worlds co-exist is proof of this. It is the source of my greatest pride and my darkest disappointments. For I too am of two worlds, and it is only my love for Arthur that keeps me in this one."

images.label: Court of Aquaman - Of Two Worlds

sections.title: Part 6: Of Two Minds
items: Zone: Spindrift Station
Instance: Starro: Spindrift Station
Location:

Briefing: Mera:" The Court of Atlantis sees Arthur as a savior when it suits them and a pariah when it does not. Many of the old guard still believe he is ill suited, but their beliefs never find their way to words in my company."

images.label: Court of Aquaman - Of Two Minds

sections.title: Part 7: Sea of Politics
items: Zone: Spindrift Station
Instance: Starro: Spindrift Station
Location:

Briefing: Mera:" If it were up to me I would clean house of all but the most loyal of Arthur's court. Let the politicians and traditionalists earn a real living. While Arthur and I protect both land and sea, they squabble and critique. To the abyss with them all!"

images.label: Court of Aquaman - Sea of Politics

items: Upon completion of this briefing players receive a message from Mera, accessible from any Mail Terminal.

table.caption: Mail Messages
rows: " Being the King of two thirds of the Earth is a never-ending struggle for Arthur. But he does so without a thought, giving himself to both peoples below and above the surface. And I will be there, at his side, always."

title: Deathstroke's Contract (Briefings)
summary: Deathstroke's Contract is a global briefing introduced in the Lightning Strikes DLC. There are 9 parts than comprise this briefing.

sections.title: Overview
items: Deathstroke's Contract is a global briefing introduced in the Lightning Strikes DLC. There are 9 parts than comprise this briefing.

sections.title: Synopsis
items: " Deathstroke, assassin for hire extraordinaire, has a list of targets he has been contacted to eliminate."

sections.title: Part 1: Deathstroke's Contract: The Flash
items: Zone: Central City
Region: Central City
Location: At the base of Flash's statue on the center of the park.

Investigation: Deathstroke: "Target Alpha. Designation - The Flash. This target is an apex speedster - the top of the food chain. Introducing a distraction such as a threat to the public will decrease target's combat reaction time by 18%. Planned hazards such as explosive caltrops or gravity dampening devices will increase this to 27%."

sections.title: Part 2: Deathstroke's Contract: Black Lightning
items: Zone: Central City
Region: Central City
Location: Under the highway leading to Iron Heights, next to a Bessolo.

Investigation: Deathstroke: "Target Bravo. Designation - Black Lightning. Olympic level athlete. Biologically generates electromagnetic fields capable of repelling ballistic assaults. Despite his peak physical condition, a bombardment of projectile attacks will drain his stamina by 46%, substantially reducing his ability to generate and utilize electricity for offensive attacks."

sections.title: Part 3: Deathstroke's Contract: Cyborg
items: Zone: Metropolis
Region: Tomorrow District
Location: Building north of STAR Labs

Investigation: Deathstroke: "Target Victor. Stone. Designation - Cyborg. With weaponized prosthetics he's got brains and brawn. Challenging his humanity will make him hesitate using his cybernetics, increasing reaction times by 322%, allowing time to deploy EMP charge. Cyberprosthetic system restore allows 4.4 seconds to eliminate organic threat."

sections.title: Part 4: Deathstroke's Contract: Raven
items: Zone: Gotham City
Region: Burnley
Location: {{{loc}}}

Investigation: Deathstroke: "Target Delta. Designation - Raven. Telekinetic telepath, makes direct attack too risky. Exploit targets self doubt, employ psychological tactics. Proper stimuli should keep her focus inward and increase combat predictability by 42%. Choice of location can elevate this to 73%."

sections.title: Part 5: Deathstroke's Contract: Donna Troy
items: Zone: Metropolis
Region: Historic District
Location: {{{loc}}}

Investigation: Deathstroke: "Target Echo. Designation - Donna Troy. The Amazon army of one. Super strength, flight and speed. Unlike apex metas, the Amazons' Achilles' heel is a dependency on respiration. A 95% drop in O2 levels will cause blackout to occur in 180 seconds. Releasing nerve agent vapor to block enzymes in the brain will paralyze target and allow time for loss of consciousness."

sections.title: Part 6: Deathstroke's Contract: Kid Flash
items: Zone: Metropolis
Region: Little Bohemia
Location: {{{loc}}}

Investigation: Deathstroke: "Target Alpha-two. Designation - Kid Flash. An impulsive speedster with a lot to prove. Sustained pushback from a concussive barrage will aggravate the overeager speedster, resulting in an 88% probability that Kid Flash will attempt to converge within .5 meters. Unprepared for a counterattack, use point blank shotgun blast to unprotected knee."

sections.title: Part 7: Deathstroke's Contract: Nightwing
items: Zone: Gotham City
Region: East End
Location: {{{loc}}}

Investigation: Deathstroke: "Target Romeo. Designation - Nightwing. This target will be extremely prepared for any fight. There is a 90% probability Nightwing's analysis of my own tactics will result in him employing misdirection. Allowing him to "win" for a time creates over confidence, leading to a 68% probability that he will fail to see a counterstroke already in place."

sections.title: Part 8: Deathstroke's Contract: Starfire
items: Zone: Metropolis
Region: Suicide Slums
Location: {{{loc}}}

Investigation: Deathstroke: "Target Juliet. Designation - Starfire. Tamaranean physiology provides Meta-level strength and flight but comes with quite the temperament. Relentless taunts will raise frustration levels and decrease precision of Starbolts by 38%. Sudden drop in accuracy will force target to overcommit and resort to ground based melee attacks. A shift to melee attacks will increase my own lethality by 24%."

sections.title: Part 9: Deathstroke's Contract: Static
items: Zone: Gotham City
Region: Burnley
Location: {{{loc}}}

Investigation: Deathstroke: "Target Tango. Designation - Static. This target relies almost completely on his ability to command electricity and magnetism. Martial threat is null. Avoiding electrically "hot" environments and restricting use of weapons to non-conductive materials will impair his over-all effectiveness by three-fold."

items: Upon completion of this briefing, players receive a message from Nightwing, accessible from any Mail Terminal.

Villains:

table.caption: Mail Messages
rows: " Deathstroke is not one to be messed with. It's good you collected this evidence of his hit list. We'll have to warn the Titans to be on the lookout."
